comment: The data of crypto's generated tables and of llms.txt; doc/tables/generate.py reads it with the test Jamfiles, the message tests and the superproject's Jamfile fixtures, and writes doc/generated/, doc/llms.txt, include/webcpp/crypto/detail/capabilities.hpp, include/webcpp/crypto/detail/defaults.hpp and test/capabilities_test.cpp. The capability table is `families`: per family its algorithms, the targets on which each backend has it (each claimed only where a test of the family's operations on that backend runs), constant time per target where it differs from the backend's own `constant_time` (X25519 on wasip2, an open finding, and natively without arm64's DIT, the cause of both), with `constant_time_checker` naming the checker that measured it where that is not every checker of the target, and the default per target, one whatever the program links (design D32), with its reason and the tests that fix it (a row of some of `compilers` restates its target's default for them, with a reason of their own, and each compiler of a target has one row), from which come include/webcpp/crypto/detail/defaults.hpp and the refusal that says what a program whose default is not linked needs; a backend with `targets`, where it is built, is a tag of `backends`. A name in a text is written between backticks, as Markdown writes code: the tables show it as code and llms.txt keeps the backticks. A comparison table's cell {speed:<family>} or {constant_time:<family>} is written from doc/performance.json or from the family's `constant_time`, and each cell of a column a namespace lists in `cited` cites a source or begins with "none". Edit this file, then run python3 libs/crypto/doc/tables/generate.py; the doc build runs it with --check.
llms: Cryptographic primitives for C++20 on native, wasip2, wasip3 and Emscripten: AES-GCM, the AES block cipher, secp256k1 (BIP 340 Schnorr, ECDSA and recoverable signatures, ECDH, tweaks, ElligatorSwift, MuSig2, silent payments), Ed25519 and Ed25519ph (RFC 8032), X25519 (RFC 7748), their keys in SPKI, PKCS#8 (RFC 8410) and PEM, P-256 key pairs, ECDSA and ECDH on BearSSL, libsodium's crypto_kx, the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEADs, libsodium's secret boxes, boxes and sealed boxes, a random_device on the system's generator, a constant_time_equal and an erase_secret whose stores the optimiser keeps, each over a widely used, reviewed C library (BearSSL, OpenSSL, ctaes, libsecp256k1, libsodium) that the program names in its Jamfile. Hashing and HMAC are Boost.Hash2's; HKDF and password hashing are webcpp::hash's. Every failure is a boost::system::result value. Protocols (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Nostr) belong to domain libraries built on these primitives.

A secp256k1 key pair: made from its 32-byte secret key, which `secret()` gives back, or drawn from `random_device`; its public key, a `curves::secp256k1::public_key`; `sign(crypto::schnorr, message)` (BIP 340, its auxiliary randomness drawn or given), `sign(crypto::ecdsa_sha256, input)` (hedged too) and `sign(crypto::ecdsa_sha256_recoverable, input)`, the input a message hashed inside or `crypto::prehashed{digest}`; ECDH in three forms, `agree` (the shared x), `agree_hashed` and `agree_point`, each with a peer's `public_key`; and the x-only tweak.

Verifies a BIP 340 signature against a `curves::secp256k1::public_key` or its 32-byte x-only form, `crypto::verify(crypto::schnorr, signature, message, key)`, or an ECDSA one against a `curves::secp256k1::public_key`, `crypto::verify(crypto::ecdsa_sha256, signature, input, public_key)`, refusing a high S; `recover(crypto::ecdsa_sha256_recoverable, signature, input)` gives the signer's key.
ECDSA's strict DER encoding, and low S as two functions, `normalize_low_s` and `is_low_s`.
Tweaks an x-only public key by a 32-byte tweak a protocol computes.
With `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE`, natively, every allocation of OpenSSL's in the process goes to a `std::pmr::memory_resource` the program defines.

An Ed25519 key pair (RFC 8032): made from a 32-byte seed, which `secret()` gives back, or drawn from `random_device`; its public key, a `curves::ed25519::public_key`; 64-byte signatures of a message with `sign(crypto::eddsa, message)`; and its X25519 secret key.

An Ed25519 public key, its 32 bytes, which `crypto::verify(crypto::eddsa, ...)` takes: made from bytes with only their size checked, since whether the point is canonical and not of small order is the verification policy's judgment.

Verifies an Ed25519 signature with a public key alone, `crypto::verify(crypto::eddsa, signature, message, public_key)`, under the policy `strict`: libsodium's rules, which refuse non-canonical encodings and keys of small order.
Ed25519ph (RFC 8032): a message given in pieces, hashed with SHA-512, then signed with a key pair or verified with `verify(signature, public_key)`.
The X25519 public key of an Ed25519 public key (the birational map), refusing a key of small order or not canonical with `invalid_public_key`.
The 32-byte X25519 public key of a 32-byte secret key (RFC 7748).
The 32-byte shared secret of a secret key and a peer's public key, a `secret<32>`, refused with `weak_public_key` when it is all zero (a peer key of low order).

RFC 8410's SPKI of an Ed25519 public key (44 bytes) and PKCS#8 of a key pair (version 1, the seed alone, 48 bytes), the forms OpenSSL and WebCrypto write, decoded strictly: any other bytes are `invalid_encoding`.

RFC 8410's SPKI of an X25519 public key (44 bytes) and PKCS#8 of a secret key (version 1, 48 bytes), the forms OpenSSL and WebCrypto write, decoded strictly into a `secret<32>`: any other bytes are `invalid_encoding`.

PEM (RFC 7468): DER as base64 between `-----BEGIN <label>-----` and `-----END <label>-----`, lines of 64 characters and line feeds, as OpenSSL writes it; read strictly, so that any other text is `invalid_encoding`.

libsodium's `crypto_kx`: a key pair made from a 32-byte seed or drawn from `random_device`, and the two session keys of a client or a server, each a `secret<32>`, from the peer's public key; a peer key of low order is refused with `weak_public_key`.
RFC 8439's ChaCha20-Poly1305, authenticated encryption in place with a 12-byte nonce.
The original ChaCha20-Poly1305, authenticated encryption in place with an 8-byte nonce a counter numbers.
XChaCha20-Poly1305, authenticated encryption in place with a 24-byte nonce safe to draw at random.
NaCl's and libsodium's `crypto_secretbox`, XSalsa20-Poly1305: authenticated encryption in place under a 32-byte key, with a 24-byte nonce safe to draw at random and no additional data.
libsodium's `crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305`: the secret box with XChaCha20 in place of XSalsa20.

NaCl's and libsodium's `crypto_box`: X25519 agrees a key once per pair of keys, refusing a peer key of small order, then XSalsa20-Poly1305 seals and opens each message in place, with a 24-byte nonce safe to draw at random.
libsodium's `crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305`: the box with XChaCha20 in place of XSalsa20.
libsodium's sealed boxes, `crypto_box_seal`: anonymous encryption to a public key under a key pair drawn per message, 48 bytes longer than the message, which only the recipient's key pair opens.

The public key that made a recoverable ECDSA signature, `recover(crypto::ecdsa_sha256_recoverable, signature, input)`, the input as signing took it: a message hashed inside or `crypto::prehashed{digest}`.

A secp256k1 public key, a point checked on the curve, which `crypto::verify` and a key pair's `agree` take: made from its compressed or uncompressed SEC 1 form, and giving its compressed, uncompressed and x-only forms.

Without DIT, dudect times `agree` with an all-zero secret key against random ones at |t| 6.7 to 14.5 (2026-11-19) and 4.3 to 7.8 (2026-11-21, three runs): about one nanosecond in 15 µs. The cause is Apple silicon's DIT (data-independent timing), which wasmtime does not set ({apple-dit}): with DIT set in wasmtime's main thread, an experiment and not the lane, the same case reads |t| 1.5 to 2.1; no branch on a secret was found in the WebAssembly or in wasmtime's compiled code. rules.title: Never reuse an IV under one key
rules.text: two AES-GCM messages under one key and one IV reveal the XOR of their plaintexts and let an attacker forge tags for every later message ({joux}; {nonce-reuse}); draw a random 12-byte IV per message, or use a counter that never repeats, a restart included.

rules.title: The usage limit
rules.text: with random IVs, at most 2^32 messages under one key ({sp800-38d}, section 8.3); rotate the key before.

rules.title: A failed open zeroes data
rules.text: when the tag does not match, `open` returns `authentication_failed` and zeroes the whole of `data`; keep a copy of the ciphertext if it is needed after a failure. the incremental open authenticates every piece and verifies the tag before it decrypts any; a stream read only once is sealed in records.

rules.title: Records: each stream its own key
rules.text: records numbered from 0 with the number as IV are safe only under a key used for that one stream: derive a key per stream (HKDF of the storage key with a random salt) or draw one; never number two streams' records under one key.

rules.title: ECDH's form
rules.text: `keypair::agree` returns the raw x coordinate of the shared point, which protocols such as Nostr's NIP-44 ({nip44}) take; `keypair::agree_hashed` returns libsecp256k1's hashed form, the SHA-256 of the compressed shared point. Both sides must use the same form, or they derive different keys. Derive keys with a KDF, never use a shared secret directly.

rules.title: The x-only tweak is not BIP 32
rules.text: `tweak_xonly` is BIP 341's even-y arithmetic ({bip341}); BIP 32's child derivation tweaks the full key, with `seckey_tweak_add` and `pubkey_tweak_add`, and computes the tweak with HMAC-SHA-512, a domain library's ({bip32}).

rules.title: Ethereum
rules.text: this version signs and verifies Ethereum's ECDSA, recoverable signatures included (`keypair::sign(crypto::ecdsa_sha256_recoverable, input)`), recovers a signer's public key from a signature and the same input (`recover`), and writes the uncompressed key ({ethereum}); the recovery id's `v` encoding, the hash Ethereum signs, transactions and addresses are a domain library's.

rules.title: Compare secrets in constant time
rules.text: compare a tag, a MAC or a token with `constant_time_equal`, never `==` or `memcmp` ({cwe208}).

rules.title: Secrets come from random_device
rules.text: keys, IVs and tokens are drawn from `random_device`, never `std::mt19937` or `rand` ({cwe338}).

rules.title: Never reuse a nonce under one ChaCha20-Poly1305 key
rules.text: two messages under one key and one nonce reveal the XOR of their plaintexts and let an attacker forge tags ({rfc8439-nonce}). `xchacha20_poly1305` and the secret boxes: draw 24 bytes at random per message. `chacha20_poly1305`: number the 12-byte nonces with a counter that never repeats, a restart included, or draw them at random for at most 2^32 messages per key, AES-GCM's bound for random 12-byte IVs ({sp800-38d}). `chacha20_poly1305_original`: a counter only, its 8 bytes are too short to draw.

rules.title: A shared secret is not a key
rules.text: derive keys from X25519's shared secret and both public keys with a KDF such as webcpp::hash's HKDF, never use its bytes as a cipher's key ({rfc7748-kdf}); `kx_keypair` and the boxes do this themselves.

rules.title: The default on MSVC is not constant time
rules.text: natively the default is OpenSSL, which MSVC builds no-asm, table-based ({openssl-install}); where timing attacks matter, link BearSSL and name `gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>`, and for the block cipher link ctaes and name `aes256<backends::ctaes>`.

fixes.async_from_key_xchacha: Call the synchronous `from_key`: XChaCha20-Poly1305 is not in WebCrypto, so it has no asynchronous form.
fixes.async_from_secret_secp256k1: Call the synchronous `from_secret`: secp256k1 is not in WebCrypto, so only Ed25519's and P-256's key pairs have `async_from_secret`.
fixes.make_removed: Call the factory named by its input, member or free: `from_secret` for a key pair, `from_bytes` for a public key, `from_key` for a cipher (`crypto::from_secret<K>(bytes)`, `K::from_secret(bytes)`); `make` is gone, with no alias.
fixes.hybrid_header_removed: Include `<webcpp/crypto/public_key_encryption/box.hpp>` for `box` and `box_xchacha20poly1305`, `<webcpp/crypto/public_key_encryption/sealed_box.hpp>` for `sealed_box`, `<webcpp/crypto/key_exchange/kx.hpp>` for `kx_keypair`; the old directory is kept free for post-quantum hybrids.
fixes.hybrid_names_removed: Name `crypto::public_key_encryption::box`, `box_xchacha20poly1305` and `sealed_box`, and `crypto::key_exchange::kx_keypair` and `session_keys`; `crypto::hybrid` and the names in `curves::x25519` are gone, with no alias.
fixes.async_seal_xchacha: Call the AEAD's own `seal`: only AES-GCM has `async_seal`.
fixes.async_open_xchacha: Call the AEAD's own `open`: only AES-GCM has `async_open`.
fixes.async_sign_secp256k1: Call the key pair's own signing function: secp256k1 is not in WebCrypto, so only Ed25519's and P-256's key pairs have `async_sign`.
fixes.async_sign_ed25519_prehashed: Give `async_sign` the message itself with `crypto::eddsa`, RFC 8032's pure Ed25519, which takes no digest, as the synchronous `sign` does.
fixes.async_sign_p256_eddsa: Give `async_sign` the key pair's own scheme: `crypto::ecdsa_sha256` for a P-256 key pair, `crypto::eddsa` for an Ed25519 key pair.
fixes.async_verify_named_backend: As `async_verify_wrong_key`: naming the backend does not add a scheme; call `crypto::verify` for `crypto::schnorr` and secp256k1's keys.
fixes.async_verify_wrong_key: Call `crypto::verify` for a key the asynchronous family lacks (secp256k1's, Schnorr's x-only key): `async_verify` has a `curves::ed25519::public_key` with `crypto::eddsa` and a `curves::p256::basic_public_key` with `crypto::ecdsa_sha256`.
fixes.prehashed_dynamic: Give `crypto::prehashed` a digest of a fixed size: a `std::array<std::uint8_t, 32>`, a `std::span<std::uint8_t const, 32>` or a `boost::hash2::digest<32>`.
fixes.sign_p256_schnorr: Sign with `crypto::ecdsa_sha256`, P-256's scheme; BIP340's `crypto::schnorr` is secp256k1's.
fixes.sign_ed25519_ecdsa: Sign with `crypto::eddsa`, Ed25519's scheme; `crypto::ecdsa_sha256` is P-256's and secp256k1's.
fixes.sign_ed25519_prehashed: Sign the message itself with `crypto::eddsa`, RFC 8032's pure Ed25519, which takes no digest; to sign a message given in pieces, use Ed25519ph, `curves::ed25519::ph<webcpp::hash::sha2_512>`.
fixes.sign_schnorr_prehashed: Sign the message itself with `crypto::schnorr`, BIP340's, which has no prehash mode; a taproot sighash, BIP341's tagged hash, is that message.
fixes.sign_secp256k1_eddsa: Sign with `crypto::ecdsa_sha256`, `crypto::ecdsa_sha256_recoverable` or `crypto::schnorr`, secp256k1's schemes; `crypto::eddsa` is Ed25519's.
fixes.sign_secp256k1_not_a_scheme: Name the scheme with its tag: `crypto::ecdsa_sha256`, `crypto::ecdsa_sha256_recoverable` or `crypto::schnorr`.
fixes.verify_ecdsa_bytes_key: Give `crypto::ecdsa_sha256` the public key as a typed object, `curves::secp256k1::public_key::from_bytes(bytes)` or `curves::p256::public_key::from_bytes(bytes)`: bytes never choose the curve.
fixes.verify_eddsa_bytes_key: Give `crypto::eddsa` the public key as a `curves::ed25519::public_key`: `key_pair.public_key()`, or `curves::ed25519::public_key::from_bytes(bytes)` for a key received as bytes.
fixes.async_verify_eddsa_bytes_key: Give `async_verify` with `crypto::eddsa` the public key as a `curves::ed25519::public_key`, as `crypto::verify` takes it: `key_pair.public_key()`, or `curves::ed25519::public_key::from_bytes(bytes)`.
fixes.sign_free_ed25519_ecdsa: As `sign_ed25519_ecdsa`: `crypto::sign` calls the key pair's own `sign`, so sign with `crypto::eddsa`, Ed25519's scheme.
fixes.sign_free_public_key: Give `crypto::sign` the key pair, whose public key verifies: `crypto::sign(key_pair, scheme, input)`, then `crypto::verify(scheme, signature, input, public_key)` or `public_key.verify(scheme, signature, input)`.
fixes.verify_member_eddsa_prehashed: Verify the message itself with `crypto::eddsa`, RFC 8032's pure Ed25519, which takes no digest, as `crypto::verify` does; a message given in pieces is Ed25519ph's, `curves::ed25519::ph<webcpp::hash::sha2_512>`.
fixes.verify_member_ed25519_ecdsa: Verify with `crypto::eddsa`, Ed25519's scheme; `crypto::ecdsa_sha256` is P-256's and secp256k1's, whose keys are `curves::p256::basic_public_key` and `curves::secp256k1::public_key`.
fixes.verify_member_secp256k1_recoverable: Give a recoverable signature to `curves::secp256k1::recover(crypto::ecdsa_sha256_recoverable, signature, input)`, which gives the signer's key; a public key verifies `crypto::ecdsa_sha256` and `crypto::schnorr`.
fixes.verify_free_secp256k1_recoverable: As `verify_member_secp256k1_recoverable`: give a recoverable signature to `curves::secp256k1::recover`, which gives the signer's key; `crypto::verify` takes `crypto::ecdsa_sha256` and `crypto::schnorr` with a secp256k1 key.
fixes.verify_member_p256_eddsa: Verify with `crypto::ecdsa_sha256`, P-256's scheme; `crypto::eddsa` is Ed25519's, whose key is a `curves::ed25519::public_key`.
fixes.verify_p256_secp256k1_signature: Give a P-256 key a `curves::p256::ecdsa_signature`, made from the 64 bytes received with `curves::p256::ecdsa_signature::from_bytes`; a secp256k1 signature verifies with a `curves::secp256k1::public_key`.
fixes.verify_schnorr_as_ecdsa: Verify a BIP340 signature with `crypto::schnorr`, its scheme; `crypto::ecdsa_sha256` takes a `curves::secp256k1::ecdsa_signature`, which `sign(crypto::ecdsa_sha256, input)` gives.
fixes.verify_ed25519_bytes_signature: Make the 64 bytes received into a `curves::ed25519::signature` with `curves::ed25519::signature::from_bytes`, which checks their size, and verify that.
fixes.recover_ecdsa_signature: Give `recover` a `curves::secp256k1::recoverable_signature`, which `sign(crypto::ecdsa_sha256_recoverable, input)` gives, or made from 65 bytes with `from_bytes`; an ECDSA signature without its recovery id verifies with `crypto::verify` and the signer's public key.
fixes.async_verify_p256_bytes_signature: As `verify_p256_secp256k1_signature`: make the 64 bytes received into a `curves::p256::ecdsa_signature` with `from_bytes`, then give it to `async_verify`.
fixes.agree_free_wrong_peer: Give `agree` the peer's typed public key of the key pair's own curve and backend: `curves::p256::basic_public_key<Backend>::from_bytes(bytes)` for P-256, `curves::secp256k1::public_key::from_bytes(bytes)` for secp256k1.

fixes.sign_p256_digest_48: Give `crypto::ecdsa_sha256` SHA-256's 32-byte digest, `crypto::prehashed{digest}` of a `std::array<std::uint8_t, 32>`, or the message itself, which it hashes.
fixes.sign_secp256k1_recoverable_digest_48: As `sign_p256_digest_48`: give `crypto::ecdsa_sha256_recoverable` SHA-256's 32-byte digest, or the message itself, which it hashes.

fixes.erase_secret_const_range: Erase the buffer the secret was written to, through a non-const reference to it (`std::string&`, `std::span<std::byte>`): a const view cannot be erased. Its elements must be trivially copyable, bytes or integers; a range of `std::string` or of another type with its own storage cannot be erased as bytes, so erase each element's buffer instead.
